description: Hand-recorded Task A5 log. Times are wall-clock timestamps captured with `date` in the terminal while the migration was performed by the coding agent (Claude Code), so they measure an AI agent with full context, NOT a human engineer. The objective, reproducible measures are the change sizes and the test/mutation results in migration_report.json.
precondition: FY 2025-26 expected values (128 cases) were generated by the independent oracle BEFORE any engine was migrated (test-first). Before migration all three engines raised RuleSetNotFound for FY 2025-26 (see migration_before.json).

steps.what: New rule-text corpus project_a/rule_texts/fy2025_26.yaml: passages copied, P25-NEW-SLABS and P25-87A replaced with the AY 2026-27 official text (87A with Finance Act 2025 substitutions applied).
New file config/tax_rules_fy2025_26.yaml: new-regime slab table (6 rows -> 7 rows) and NEW.87A income_limit/max_rebate changed; clause/source metadata updated. No Python changes.
steps.result: 128/128 FY 2025-26 cases rupee-exact on first run; FY 2024-25 still 179/179

steps.what: No code change: retrieval selects passages by financial year, so the new corpus is the whole migration.
steps.result: Measured later (2026-11-09) with real calls, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, 40 random cases per year: FY 2025-26 rupee-exact 30% (12/40), FY 2024-25 25%; its shadow check rejected every wrong answer. No code change was needed, but the migration cannot be verified without a rule engine checking every answer.
steps.result_at_migration_time: NOT VERIFIED: no GEMINI_API_KEY, so FY 2025-26 accuracy of the query-time LLM could not be measured. Known risk (unmeasured): the model's training data contains both years' slabs.

steps.what: Built compile_prompt_fy2025_26.txt, regenerated the artifact (LLM = Claude in the dev session), static validation, suite verification, 20k-profile differential vs Engine A, approval.
steps.result: validation 0 problems; 128/128 cases; 0/20,000 differential mismatches; approved

what_broke: Nothing broke in Engines A or C: both were built with per-year rule sets and fail-loud lookup, and the FY 2025-26 tests existed before the change.

Engine B needed no code change (retrieval is by financial year), but it could not be verified at migration time (no key then). Measured later with real calls: 30% rupee-exact on FY 2025-26 (40-case sample) - an LLM migration is only as safe as the rule engine that checks it.
silent_failure_findings: Year-blind behaviour (answering FY 2025-26 with FY 2024-25 law) would be silently wrong on 101/128 = 78.9% of FY 2025-26 cases with 0 errors raised (silent_failure_probe). All three engines are protected because they raise RuleSetNotFound instead of falling back.

Compiled-artifact hazard: the 87A threshold literal appears 3 times in one expression; updating only 1 of 3 is caught by just 7/128 cases (all in the 12L-12.7L marginal-relief band). Without those boundary cases this would ship silently.

Official-source hazard: the Income Tax Department 'Computation of tax for individual' page states the AY 2026-27 Rs 60,000 rebate applies 'up to Rs 7,00,000'; the statute (Finance Act 2025) and the 'Brief on budget' page say Rs 12,00,000. A pipeline (or LLM retrieval) reading that page would silently produce a wrong rebate. We cite the 87A section text (ITD-87A-FA2025) instead.
Equivalent mutant: changing the old-regime 87A maximum to 60,000 has no behavioural effect (old-regime tax at total income <= 5L is at most 12,500), so no test can or should catch it.
